sources.producer: CSU Monterey Bay Seafloor Mapping Lab
sources.reason: Original grids were inspected, but NAVD88 elevations are not qualified MLLW fishing depths. The habitat grid codes rough versus smooth terrain inferred from bathymetry, not sampled rock. The metadata's positional/vertical accuracy statements vary with depth and are not per-cell product uncertainty. No target or export may be generated from this source until datum, substrate, hazards and complete legal geometry are reviewed.

bathymetry.process_description: Bathymetric data were post-processed using CARIS HIPS hydrographic data cleaning system software. Applanix POSPAC software (v 5.3) was used to process the logged POS M/V files and create a Smoothed Best Estimated Trajectory (SBET) composed of an integrated inertial/GPS solution for use in horizontal and vertical positioning of sounding data. Correction for vertical oscillation due to heave and tide was accomplished using these SBET files. Final x,y,z soundings, surface models, and derived products are relative to the NAVD88 Geoid09 vertical datum. Raw Reson s7k survey data was converted to HDCS format within CARIS HIPS. Erroneous soundings were removed via basic filtering and detailed swath and subset cleaning; the remaining high-confidence soundings were used in surface model creation and final product generation. Soundings (x,y,z) were exported from a Combined Uncertainty and Bathymetry Estimator (CUBE) Surface as an ASCII file with 1m (or 2m) spacing. The 1m (or 2m) decimated x,y,z ASCII text file was imported into Fledermaus AverageGridder to create digital elevation model (DEM) grid(s). The 1m (or 2m) Fledermaus grid was exported as an ArcInfo ASCII raster file (.asc), which was imported into ArcGIS Spatial Analyst to generate a 1m (or 2m, 5m, 10m) bathymetry ArcInfo grid. The Spatial Analyst Surface Analysis tools were then used to produce hillshade and slope grids from the 2m (5m, 10m) bathymetry grid. Post-survey data cleaning, CUBE surface creation, and final products derived from post-processed multibeam bathymetry data were applied by the Seafloor Mapping Lab at CSUMB.
bathymetry.horizontal_accuracy_text: ±2 m horizontal, but varies with depth
bathymetry.vertical_accuracy_text: ± 20 cm vertical, but varies with depth

terrain_habitat.process_description: Rough and smooth habitat areas determined by surface:planar area (SA:PA) ratio and/or vector ruggedness analyses of the bathymetric DEM (see Substrate_Analysis metadata for more information) were stratified by depth zones to produce depth-stratified habitat grids. Depth zones used were 0 - -30m, -30 - -100m, -100 - -200m, and <= -200m. Cell values in the depth-stratified habitat grid signify both depth zone and substrate as follows: 0 Depth = 0- -30, Substrate = Smooth -1 Depth = 0- -30, Substrate = Rough -30 Depth = -30- -100, Substrate = Smooth -31 Depth = -30- -100, Substrate = Rough -100 Depth = -100 - -200, Substrate = Smooth -101 Depth = -100 - -200, Substrate = Rough -200 Depth <= -200, Substrate = Smooth -201 Depth <= -200, Substrate = Rough The masking process used in the initial creation of the substrate data layer, which was used to minimize misclassification due to noise and artifacts, produces a conservative estimate of total rough (potential rock) substrate, especially in deeper locations such as canyon walls and the steeply sloped continental margin. In these areas, increased noise and high slope can confound the area ratio-based substrate classification, so a vector ruggedness measure was employed in place of the standard SA:PA ratio analyses.
